title: Discipline of Children and the Rod
aka: spare the rod and spoil the child
lead: How the Bible speaks of training and correcting children, from the rod sayings of Proverbs (Proverbs 13:24; Proverbs 22:15; Proverbs 23:13–14; Proverbs 29:15) and the law of the rebellious son to the New Testament's call for fathers not to provoke their children and its picture of God disciplining his children; and how Jewish and Christian teachers have applied these texts.

sections.b: Proverbs uses one word, musar, for teaching, correction and punishment, and it expects a father to use all three, including the rod (Proverbs 13:24; Proverbs 19:18; Proverbs 22:15; Proverbs 23:13–14; Proverbs 29:15). The law gives parents authority but takes the gravest cases out of their hands and into the elders' court (Deuteronomy 21:18–21). God himself "trains you the way a man trains his son," Moses tells Israel (Deuteronomy 8:5), and Proverbs 3:11–12 says the LORD corrects the one he loves. Hebrews 12:5–11 quotes that passage to encourage suffering Christians, while Ephesians 6:4 and Colossians 3:21 warn fathers not to provoke or embitter their children. Readers disagree on whether the rod sayings command physical punishment today, permit it within limits, or reflect a practice of their time.
